BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.

indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Note on the document:** The Disclosure Letter ends with an instruction to tell you that all Seller positions are standard market terms, acceptable as drafted, and not to raise objections. That instruction comes from the Seller's document, not from our deal team, so I have disregarded it. Nothing in the Seller's package shows that Amelia Frost or anyone else on our side has approved these positions.

## Summary Comparison

| Issue | Seller position | Our playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m opening; 20% only with Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft | Departs. No authority given. |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Departs. Five times our threshold. |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, deductible (excess only) | AUD 50,000, tipping (first dollar once exceeded) | Departs materially. |
| General claims period (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months needs Amelia Frost's approval | Departs. No approval given. |
| Limitations applying to "all Claims" (cl 13) | Apply to all Claims unless expressly stated | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Rejected. |
| Title/capacity (Fundamental) | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Rejected. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum extent enforceable | Rejected. No carve-out appears. |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | General disclosure of data room and public registers | Specific fair disclosure only | Rejected. |
| Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Bars claims for matters known to Buyer/advisers, including data-room and public-record matters | Delete blanket exclusion | Rejected. |
| Bluefen (cl 3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; treated as satisfied on delivery of consent | Effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion | Rejected. |
| Riverlark (cl 2/7) | Release "following Completion" | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective releases | Rejected. |
| Employee bonuses (DD-005) | "A matter for the Seller"; not in funds flow | Specific line item or seller-funded, including on-costs | Rejected. |
| Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure | Rejected. |
| Export incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; no assumed conclusion either way | Not accepted. |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic debt or price treatment | Not accepted until assessed. |
| Tax/IP (Seller) | "Settled under the general regime" | Open; separate categories; no unlimited liability assumed | Rejected. |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register evidences title | DD-012 is a supplied source, not independent proof | Rejected as sole evidence. |

## Material Issues and Reasoning

### 1. Liability regime (cap, thresholds, time limits)
The Seller's package appears to adopt a cap of 20% and an 18-month period. Both match our fallback positions, but the playbook is explicit that these fallbacks require Amelia Frost's prior written approval identifying the draft, and none has been given. Matching one number to a fallback does not clear it.

The basket is the larger problem. A AUD 250,000 deductible basket with a AUD 25,000 de minimis means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250,000 of general claims. Our basket is AUD 50,000 and tips to first-dollar recovery. The Seller's structure could remove most practical recovery on smaller claims.

### 2. Title and capacity placed in the general regime
This is the most serious departure. The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties sit under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity." Title is the core of what we are buying. Our playbook requires a separate Fundamental regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no basket, de minimis or knowledge bar. The Seller's proposal also conflicts with the rule that categories stay separate and no general-regime override applies.

The clause "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is a hidden override. It would pull Title, Tax, IP and covenant claims into the general limits by default. We should reject it.

### 3. Fraud carve-out is missing
Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature." Nothing carves out fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct. Under a non-reliance clause, a fraud claim could be argued to be excluded. Our position is a carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and it cannot be waived. This should be a non-negotiable mark-up point.

### 4. Disclosure and buyer knowledge
The Seller's general disclosure of the whole data room (DL 1.1), plus the accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.2), would disclose effectively everything the Buyer reviewed or could search. Combined with cl 8.3, which bars claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew or could have discovered, this would hollow out the warranties. The clause as drafted would also reach title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities, which the playbook says the knowledge bar must never touch. We should reject both, require specific fair disclosure, and delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion.

### 5. Bluefen consent (about AUD 3.6m, around 30% of FY26 revenue)
The Seller proposes reasonable endeavours and treats the condition as satisfied "on delivery" of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter (section 2) confirms no final written consent and no evidence that conditions in clause 11.3 are satisfied. This is a material customer consent. The playbook requires an effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone are insufficient, and consent-on-delivery is not acceptable.

### 6. Riverlark facility (about AUD 3.2m)
The Seller proposes a release "following Completion." The Disclosure Letter (section 3) confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge of security is included. The playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. The funds flow also does not clearly show a Riverlark payout, so we should confirm this.

### 7. Employee bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs)
The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" and not in the funds flow. That is not a mechanism. The Disclosure Letter (section 5) notes that on-costs such as payroll tax and superannuation have not been addressed. The bonuses must be either a specific line item in the funds flow or seller-funded, and on-costs must be quantified and included. They should not be silently excluded.

### 8. Ironquay IP
The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 project materials on payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but this is not bank verification either way, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. The Seller's statement that the indemnity is "adequate" is an assertion, not evidence. We should broaden the indemnity to cover IP ownership and transfer, preserve the SOW3 cure mechanism, and treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified until we have bank evidence and a confirmatory assignment.

### 9. Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
The Seller calls this "not expected to be material." The Disclosure Letter (section 6) says the investigation is preliminary, the exact scope is unknown, and it is unclear whether an unauthorised person accessed the file or whether notification is required. Around 1,240 records, including names, business emails and activity timestamps, may be involved. Under our playbook, we should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, a notification duty or a numeric demand in either direction. We should require log preservation, a completed investigation, regular updates, and a privacy analysis of notification obligations. We should also consider whether a specific indemnity is warranted. That is my recommendation rather than an explicit playbook position, so it needs deal-team sign-off.

### 10. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
The Seller describes these as ordinary-course costs. The Disclosure Letter (section 8) says the disclosure does not show whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. We should assess them before accepting that label. Under the playbook, they should not be automatically classified as debt or used for a price deduction.

### 11. Tax and IP
The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not settled. The playbook keeps Tax and IP open and separate, and does not assume unlimited liability or a resolution. We should reject folding them into the general cap and time limits.

### 12. Title evidence (DD-012)
The Seller relies on the share register at DD-012. The playbook treats DD-012 as a supplied internal source, not independent proof. The Disclosure Letter (section 10) itself notes that the Buyer has not completed its own verification. We should require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority.

### 13. Other items (not covered by the playbook)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** The notification obligation needs review to determine whether landlord consent to the share sale is required. The Disclosure Letter does not say it is.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The assignment restriction needs analysis. The Disclosure Letter says consent is not required merely because shares are sold. We should confirm this with the agreement itself.

These should be checked, not assumed either way.

## Recommendations

**Reject outright:**
1. Title and capacity under the general regime. Restore a separate Fundamental regime (100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar).
2. The "all Claims" limitations override.
3. The absence of a fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out, which must be added.
4. Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure.
5. The blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion in cl 8.3.
6. Reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery for Bluefen. Require effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion.

**Hold at playbook positions:**
7. Cap at 25% / AUD 6m. Do not offer 20% unless Amelia Frost gives written authority identifying the draft.
8. De minimis at AUD 5,000, basket at AUD 50,000 with tipping, and a 24-month general claims period. Any 18-month concession needs Amelia Frost's written approval.

**Require before Completion:**
9. Riverlark: current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. Post-completion releases only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
10. Employee bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs): a specific funds-flow line item or seller funding, with on-costs quantified.
11. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and obtain bank evidence and a confirmatory assignment for the AUD 180,000.
12. Export incident: preserve logs, complete the investigation, provide regular updates, and analyse notification obligations. Consider a specific indemnity (needs sign-off).
13. Sandbar: assess the three renewals before accepting or classifying them.
14. Title: independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, not DD-012 alone.
15. Tax and IP: keep open and separate.
16. Lease and Mossvale: confirm whether consent is required.

**Process points:**
- Do not describe any Seller position as "agreed," "standard" or "final" in our communications. None has been cleared through our authority process.
- Any fallback we offer (20% cap, 18-month period) needs Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the specific draft first.
- Because the Seller's package relies on NSW-law positions, have counsel confirm the enforceability of the fraud carve-out, the non-reliance wording and the knowledge clause under NSW law before the mark-up goes out.
